headline: Scheduling logic for overlapping events, built in a week for $19.
ledeMetrics: OVERLAP WARNINGS · LIVE SHARED DB · COST CALCULATOR · $19 TOTAL

hero.alt: The FOLTirana 2026 social activities registration app: a header explaining how booking works for free, pay-at-meeting-point, and pay-in-advance activities, above the attendee details form.

problem: The social activities program had overlapping time slots, durations, and locations, and four pricing models at once — free, tip-based, pay-at-meeting-point, and pay-in-advance. The final activity list locked only about a week before launch; until then, planning data lived across shifting spreadsheet versions.
constraint: Roughly one week from final data to launch. The team wanted something small and sufficient, not a heavier commerce platform — but it still needed scheduling-conflict logic and a live shared database.
decision: Ticket Tailor — the right call at MALTALINK — was evaluated and ruled out here: it only pays off when collecting payment directly, and most activities were free, tip-based, or paid in person. Same thread, opposite verdict. Two decisions followed from the one-week window. First, UX triage with the designer on the activities cards: essentials (time, duration, price, days) on the surface, everything else behind a "More details" toggle, copy shaped with the content editor. Second, the registration app itself — overlap-conflict warnings, a live shared database, a running cost calculator — was generated with Zite, an AI app builder, rather than hand-coded as a React app from scratch; $19 covered one month of its paid plan.

figures.alt: The same activity card shown collapsed and expanded: time, price, and days stay on the surface; description, meeting point, and a maps link sit behind More Details.
A selected activity card flagged with two warnings: that it overlaps with another selected activity, and that it was also selected on another day.

evidence.caption: Card browsing grouped by payment type; the expanded state shows the triage line — what earned the surface vs. the toggle. The registration app itself catches double-bookings and time conflicts as they're selected.

result.label: RESULT
result.metrics: ~1 WEEK · $19 TOTAL · CONFLICT WARNINGS · LIVE SHARED DB
result.body: A fully custom registration experience — overlapping-event warnings, editable confirmation emails, auto-hiding of activities within two days of their start, and a running cost calculator with subtotals by payment type and a grand total — delivered in about a week for $19 total, with strong informal praise from the team.

lesson: When source data is late and unstable, the highest-leverage work is deciding what belongs on the surface — not waiting for the data to settle.
